approach.label: How I work

title.text: Human tension in, testable rules out.

approach.body: I don't hand off static screens or smooth over uncertainty. I surface real user friction, argue down weaker alternatives, encode clear refusal and recovery paths in working software or hardware, and mark what remains untested.

1.b: Field observation, failure modes, and the moments where automation overreaches human comfort.

2.b: Explicitly reject tempting shortcuts and document why the chosen boundary protects users.

3.b: Real Next.js, Electron, browser extension, or ESP32 builds — high enough fidelity to fail fast.

4.b: Separate observed evidence from synthetic benchmarks, and list what still needs user study.

intro.p2: My approach combines analytical thinking with creative problem-solving. I believe that great design emerges from deeply understanding user needs and iterating towards solutions that are both functional and delightful.

headline.text: I design interactions that help people stay oriented.

about.p1: I'm finishing my Master of Interaction Design at the University of Queensland after four years studying Computer Science in Wales. That mix makes it natural for me to sit in the gap between design intent and working software.
about.p2: Most of my favorite work lives where research, information architecture, and craft overlap. I enjoy messy, early-stage problems — before anyone agrees what the product should be — and the quiet discipline of reading transcripts until a clear mental model emerges.
about.p3: Outside the studio, I cook with too much garlic, read non-fiction about cities, and keep chipping away at Japanese. Write to me directly and I'll reply promptly.

1.b: If a study never challenges a design choice, it didn't earn its time.

2.b: The best interaction gets out of the way so people can act with confidence.

3.b: Empty states, recovery paths, and physical confirmations — that's where trust actually lives.

4.b: Writing down constraints and assumptions keeps everyone aligned long after a meeting ends.
